pointers.sentence: An old string is checked by what it says while its hasher is listed, and replaced at its user's next login (`docs/topics/auth/passwords.txt`).
`PBKDF2PasswordHasher.encode` derives the key with `pbkdf2`, which calls `hashlib.pbkdf2_hmac`, and joins the four parts (`django/contrib/auth/hashers.py:PBKDF2PasswordHasher.encode`).
`make_password` takes a password, a salt and a hasher, `"default"` unless named (`django/contrib/auth/hashers.py:make_password`).

`get_hashers` makes an instance of each class of `PASSWORD_HASHERS`, refusing one whose `algorithm` is empty with `ImproperlyConfigured`; `get_hashers_by_algorithm` indexes them by algorithm (`django/contrib/auth/hashers.py:get_hashers`).
`get_hasher` returns a hasher it is given as it is, the first of the list for `"default"`, and otherwise the hasher of that algorithm, or a `ValueError` (`django/contrib/auth/hashers.py:get_hasher`).
`identify_hasher` takes the algorithm from a stored string's part before the first `"$"` (`django/contrib/auth/hashers.py:identify_hasher`).

It first recognises the unsalted forms of ancient Django by length and form as `"unsalted_md5"` and `"unsalted_sha1"`, whose hashers Django 5.1 removed, so such a string finds none unless a project supplies one (`docs/releases/5.1.txt`).
`verify_password` answers whether the password matches the string, and whether the string should be made again (`django/contrib/auth/hashers.py:verify_password`).
The documentation warns of it and shows how to rehash old strings (`docs/topics/auth/passwords.txt`).

`django.contrib.auth.hashers.check_password` returns `verify_password`'s first answer and, when the password is right and the string due for an update, calls the setter it was given with the password (`django/contrib/auth/hashers.py:check_password`).

`AbstractBaseUser.check_password`'s setter sets the password with the default hasher and saves the `password` field alone, first clearing `AbstractBaseUser._password`, since by its comment a hash upgrade is not a password change (`django/contrib/auth/base_user.py:AbstractBaseUser.check_password`).

A subclass of `BasePasswordHasher` names its `algorithm` and implements `encode`, `decode`, `verify` and `safe_summary`, which raise `NotImplementedError` on the base (`django/contrib/auth/hashers.py:BasePasswordHasher`).

`safe_summary` gives a string's parts for display, `mask_hash` keeping six characters of the salt (two of an MD5 salt) and of the hash and a `"*"` for each of the rest (`django/contrib/auth/hashers.py:BasePasswordHasher.salt`, `django/contrib/auth/hashers.py:mask_hash`); `UserChangeForm` shows it in place of the password ([The authentication forms: `AuthenticationForm` and the password forms](user-forms.md)).

`PASSWORD_HASHERS` lists all but `BCryptPasswordHasher` and `MD5PasswordHasher`, in this order (`django/conf/global_settings.py`).*

`PBKDF2PasswordHasher.must_update` asks for a new string when the stored iterations differ from `PBKDF2PasswordHasher.iterations`, fewer or more, or the salt is short; `PBKDF2PasswordHasher.harden_runtime` runs the iterations missing (`django/contrib/auth/hashers.py:PBKDF2PasswordHasher.must_update`).

The iterations went from 1,500,000 to 1,800,000 (1,200,000 in 6.0); the documentation promises a rise with each release (`docs/releases/6.2.txt`, `docs/releases/6.1.txt`, `docs/topics/auth/passwords.txt`).

`BCryptSHA256PasswordHasher` takes its salt from bcrypt, which writes the rounds into it, and hashes the password's SHA-256 digest in hex, against the truncation of ticket 20138: `BCryptPasswordHasher`, hashing the password as given, is subject to bcrypt's limit of 72 bytes, its docstring says (`django/contrib/auth/hashers.py:BCryptSHA256PasswordHasher.encode`).
`MD5PasswordHasher` is the documentation's choice for tests that authenticate many users, where the default hasher is "rather slow by design" (`docs/topics/testing/overview.txt`).
